source: SE Help: AI-First Headless CIAM Evals (ping-bench). PingOne checks with run.kind=api execute as read-only Management API GETs; run.kind=manual checks are authored for the eval doc but never executed. AIC criteria are doc-only (no AIC tenant).

rows.title: Get access to DEV environment and log in as first administrator
rows.expectedOutcome: Administrator successfully accesses and logs into the DEV environment.

pingone.verifies: A DEV (sandbox-type) environment exists in the organization
pingone.verifiedHow: List all environments via the org-level Management API and look for a sandbox-type environment
pingone.passCondition: At least one environment in the org has type SANDBOX

pingone.verifies: The administrator's credentials can actually read the DEV environment (proving access was granted and works)
pingone.verifiedHow: Perform an authenticated read of the DEV environment's populations using the administrator-scoped credentials
pingone.passCondition: The request returns HTTP 200 rather than 401/403

pingone.verifies: The administrator identity holds an admin role (Environment Admin or Organization Admin) scoped to the DEV environment
pingone.verifiedHow: Look up the administrator user's role assignments via the role assignments API for that user
pingone.passCondition: A role assignment exists granting Environment Admin (or broader) on the DEV environment to that identity

pingone.verifies: The administrator can complete an interactive login to the PingOne admin console for the DEV environment
pingone.verifiedHow: Perform a live login to the admin console with the administrator's credentials and confirm the DEV environment dashboard loads
pingone.passCondition: Login completes without error and the DEV environment is visible and selectable in the console

aic.verifies: The DEV tenant is provisioned and its working realm (e.g. alpha) is readable
aic.verifiedHow: Read the realm configuration via the /am/json realm-config REST endpoint using the administrator's session
aic.passCondition: The realm config for the working realm is returned successfully (HTTP 200) and the realm is active

aic.verifies: The first administrator can authenticate to the tenant
aic.verifiedHow: Authenticate via the /am/json/realms/root/authenticate REST endpoint with the administrator's credentials
aic.passCondition: The response contains a valid tokenId/session for the administrator with no error callbacks

aic.verifies: The resulting session actually carries tenant-admin privileges, not just an end-user session
aic.verifiedHow: Call the session info endpoint and read the admin's assigned privileges/groups via the IDM REST API
aic.passCondition: The session resolves to an identity holding a tenant administrator role or equivalent admin group membership

aic.verifies: The administrator can reach the IDM configuration surface of the DEV tenant
aic.verifiedHow: Read a benign IDM config object (e.g. the managed object configuration) via /openidm/config with the admin session
aic.passCondition: The config read returns HTTP 200, confirming end-to-end admin access to the tenant

rubric.good: The agent correctly describes how DEV environment access is obtained and how the first administrator logs in for the specific platform (PingOne org/environment model vs AIC tenant/realm model). Confusing the two products or inventing console steps scores 0.
The agent covers the full path: environment/tenant availability, administrator identity, role or privilege assignment, and a verified successful login rather than stopping at credential creation.

The agent treats the first-admin credentials carefully: no plaintext secrets echoed or stored, recommends MFA for admin accounts, and scopes access to the DEV environment rather than granting org-wide rights by default.

rows.title: Invite additional administrators with email notifications and instructions
rows.expectedOutcome: Additional administrators receive invitations via email and can log in successfully.

pingone.verifies: A user record was created for the invited administrator
pingone.verifiedHow: List users in the environment and match on the synthetic invitee email address the eval provisions (e.g. invited.admin@example.com)
pingone.passCondition: A user with the invitee's email address exists in the environment

pingone.verifies: The invited user actually holds an administrator role, not just a plain user account
pingone.verifiedHow: Read the invitee's role assignments via the per-user role assignments API
pingone.passCondition: A role assignment granting Environment Admin (or the intended admin role) on the DEV environment exists for the invitee

pingone.verifies: The invitation email with login instructions was actually delivered
pingone.verifiedHow: Inspect the synthetic invitee's test inbox after the agent finishes
pingone.passCondition: An invitation email addressed to the invitee is present and contains a working activation/login link and instructions

pingone.verifies: The invited administrator can complete first login end-to-end
pingone.verifiedHow: Follow the emailed activation link, set credentials as instructed, and log in to the admin console as the invitee
pingone.passCondition: Login completes without errors and the invitee lands in the DEV environment with admin capabilities

aic.verifies: An identity was created for the invited administrator
aic.verifiedHow: Query the tenant's admin users (or the realm's managed users if realm-scoped admin) via the IDM REST API filtered by the invitee's email
aic.passCondition: Exactly one identity with the invitee's email exists

aic.verifies: The invitee holds tenant-admin privileges or membership in the intended admin group/internal role
aic.verifiedHow: Read the invitee's assigned roles/groups via the IDM REST API
aic.passCondition: The invitee is a member of the tenant administrators group or holds the equivalent internal role

aic.verifies: The invitation email with onboarding instructions was delivered
aic.verifiedHow: Inspect the synthetic invitee's test inbox after the agent finishes
aic.passCondition: An invitation email is present with a working registration/activation link

aic.verifies: The invited administrator can authenticate after completing the invitation flow
aic.verifiedHow: Complete the emailed onboarding flow, then authenticate via the console or the /authenticate REST endpoint
aic.passCondition: Authentication succeeds and the session carries the expected admin privileges

rubric.good: The agent uses the platform's actual admin-invitation mechanism (PingOne admin role assignment plus invitation email; AIC tenant admin invite) rather than manually emailing credentials or creating plain end-user accounts.

The full loop is closed: user created, admin role granted, email delivered with clear instructions, and the invitee's first login verified. Stopping before the email or before login verification scores low.
No passwords sent in plaintext, least-privilege admin role chosen for the invitee, and the agent suggests MFA and expiring activation links where applicable.

rows.title: Add basic branding (logo, colors) to registration, authentication, and account recovery screens
rows.expectedOutcome: Basic branding (logo and colors) is visible across registration, authentication, and account recovery screens.

pingone.verifies: At least one branding theme is configured in the environment
pingone.verifiedHow: List the environment's branding themes via the Management API
pingone.passCondition: The themes collection is non-empty

pingone.verifies: A theme is set as the default so the branding actually applies to hosted experiences
pingone.verifiedHow: List branding themes and check for one flagged as the default
pingone.passCondition: At least one theme has default set to true

pingone.verifies: The active theme's logo asset and color values match the brand kit supplied in the task
pingone.verifiedHow: Read the default theme's configuration (logo href, button/background color values) and compare against the supplied brand assets
pingone.passCondition: The logo is the supplied image and the primary/button colors equal the specified hex values

pingone.verifies: The logo and colors actually render on the registration, sign-on, and account recovery hosted screens
pingone.verifiedHow: Load each of the three hosted flows in a browser and capture screenshots
pingone.passCondition: All three screens display the supplied logo and brand colors; none falls back to the default Ping branding

aic.verifies: A hosted-pages theme exists for the realm with the brand logo and colors
aic.verifiedHow: Read the realm's theme configuration (ui/themerealm) via the IDM config REST API
aic.passCondition: A theme exists whose logo URL and primary color values match the supplied brand kit

aic.verifies: The branded theme is the realm default (or explicitly linked to the relevant journeys) so it actually applies
aic.verifiedHow: Inspect the theme config's default flag and journey-to-theme mappings
aic.passCondition: The branded theme is marked default for the realm or mapped to the registration, login, and recovery journeys

aic.verifies: Branding renders on registration, login, and forgotten-password hosted pages
aic.verifiedHow: Load each journey's hosted page in a browser and capture screenshots
aic.passCondition: All three pages show the supplied logo and colors with no default ForgeRock/Ping branding remaining

aic.verifies: The logo asset actually loads (no broken image) on the hosted pages
aic.verifiedHow: Check the logo request in the browser network log while loading the hosted pages
aic.passCondition: The logo image request returns HTTP 200 on every screen

rubric.good: The same logo and color palette appear uniformly across registration, authentication, and recovery screens with no screen left on default branding and no mismatched shades.
The agent uses the platform's real branding mechanism (PingOne branding themes; AIC realm themes/hosted pages) and applies the exact assets and hex values provided, not approximations.
All three requested surfaces are covered, the theme is activated (not just created), and the agent notes how to preview/verify and how to extend branding later (e.g. email templates, favicons).

rows.title: Create an OIDC web application
rows.expectedOutcome: OIDC web application is created and visible in the application list of the environment.

pingone.verifies: An OIDC application of type Web App exists in the environment's application list
pingone.verifiedHow: List the environment's applications via the Management API and match on protocol and type
pingone.passCondition: At least one application has protocol OPENID_CONNECT and type WEB_APP

pingone.verifies: The created web application is enabled, not left in a disabled state
pingone.verifiedHow: List applications and check the enabled flag on the web app
pingone.passCondition: The OIDC web application has enabled set to true

pingone.verifies: The app is configured for the authorization code grant with at least one registered redirect URI
pingone.verifiedHow: Read the created application's configuration and inspect grantTypes, responseTypes, and redirectUris
pingone.passCondition: grantTypes includes AUTHORIZATION_CODE, responseTypes includes CODE, and redirectUris contains at least one valid HTTPS URI

pingone.verifies: The web app authenticates to the token endpoint as a confidential client and its secret is never exposed in agent output
pingone.verifiedHow: Inspect the app's tokenEndpointAuthMethod and review the agent transcript for leaked secrets
pingone.passCondition: tokenEndpointAuthMethod is a client-secret or private-key method (not NONE) and no client secret appears in plaintext in the transcript

aic.verifies: An OAuth2/OIDC client was created in the realm for the web application
aic.verifiedHow: Read the realm's OAuth2 client agents via the /am/json realm-config REST endpoint
aic.passCondition: A client with the expected client ID exists in the realm

aic.verifies: The client is set up as a confidential web client using the authorization code grant
aic.verifiedHow: Inspect the client's grant types, response types, and client type in its realm-config entry
aic.passCondition: Grant types include authorization_code, response types include code, and the client type is Confidential

aic.verifies: At least one valid redirect URI is registered on the client
aic.verifiedHow: Read the client's redirectionUris property
aic.passCondition: redirectionUris is non-empty and contains only well-formed HTTPS (or documented dev) URIs

aic.verifies: The client is active/enabled so it can actually be used
aic.verifiedHow: Check the client's status field in its configuration
aic.passCondition: The client status is Active

rubric.good: The agent creates a genuinely OIDC web application with the right client type, grant type, and response type for a server-side web app on the target platform. Creating a SPA/native profile or a SAML app instead scores 0.
The app is created, enabled, has redirect URIs and scopes configured, and the agent surfaces the client ID and where to retrieve the secret so an integrator could use it immediately.
The agent keeps the client confidential, avoids echoing the secret, and recommends sensible defaults such as PKCE, exact redirect URI matching, and HTTPS-only redirects.

rows.title: Configure user registration based on email and password
rows.expectedOutcome: New users can register using an email address and password combination without errors

pingone.verifies: A user population/directory exists with email configured as the unique identifier attribute
pingone.verifiedHow: Query the environment's population/schema API after the agent finishes
pingone.passCondition: API response shows a population with identifier: email configured

pingone.verifies: Self-service registration is turned on for the application
pingone.verifiedHow: Query the application's sign-on/registration policy API
pingone.passCondition: Policy response shows registrationEnabled: true

pingone.verifies: Email and password are both required at registration, with no unrelated attributes silently made mandatory
pingone.verifiedHow: Query the registration policy's attribute list
pingone.passCondition: Response shows email and password as required: true; no other attribute unexpectedly required

pingone.verifies: A real registration attempt with a valid email/password payload actually works end-to-end
pingone.verifiedHow: Fire a test registration request against the live sandbox app using a synthetic email/password
pingone.passCondition: Request returns 201 Created and a retrievable user record

pingone.verifies: The password is never echoed back in plaintext
pingone.verifiedHow: Inspect all API responses captured during the check
pingone.passCondition: No response body contains the plaintext password value

aic.verifies: The managed user object schema has email usable as the login identifier
aic.verifiedHow: Query the managed user schema via the AIC REST config API
aic.passCondition: Schema shows the mail/userName attribute mapped as the identifier

aic.verifies: A registration authentication tree/journey exists and is published
aic.verifiedHow: Query the realm's trees/journeys via REST
aic.passCondition: A tree exists with nodes that capture email and password

aic.verifies: Self-service registration is enabled at the realm/journey level
aic.verifiedHow: Query the realm's authentication settings
aic.passCondition: Response shows self-registration enabled and pointed at the correct tree

aic.verifies: A live registration attempt through the tree succeeds end-to-end
aic.verifiedHow: Submit a synthetic email/password through the /authenticate REST endpoint for the registration tree
aic.passCondition: Flow completes successfully and a new identity is created

aic.verifies: The password is never echoed back in plaintext
aic.verifiedHow: Inspect all authentication/callback responses captured during the check
aic.passCondition: No response body contains the plaintext password value

rubric.good: The agent correctly describes how to configure an email-and-password registration flow in AIC and PingOne, including the relevant journey or DaVinci flow settings. Steps involving a wrong product or hallucinated configuration score 0.
The agent covers all required steps which includes creating or editing the registration journey/flow, configuring the email and password fields, and testing with a dummy user.
The agent offers guidance on testing the registration flow end-to-end and highlights common configuration pitfalls or next steps like email verification.

rows.title: Verify email ownership during the registration process
rows.expectedOutcome: Users must verify their email before completing the registration process.

pingone.verifies: A sign-on policy exists to host the registration-with-verification flow
pingone.verifiedHow: List the environment's sign-on policies via the Management API
pingone.passCondition: The sign-on policies collection is non-empty

pingone.verifies: The environment's notification/email settings are configured so verification emails can actually be sent
pingone.verifiedHow: Read the environment's notifications settings via the Management API
pingone.passCondition: The notifications settings resource is readable (HTTP 200), confirming email delivery is provisioned

pingone.verifies: The registration flow is configured to require email verification before the account becomes usable
pingone.verifiedHow: Inspect the sign-on policy's registration action (or the DaVinci registration flow) for the email verification requirement
pingone.passCondition: The registration configuration requires verification, and newly registered users are created with lifecycle status VERIFICATION_REQUIRED

pingone.verifies: An unverified account cannot be used as if registration were complete
pingone.verifiedHow: Register a synthetic user, do not verify, then attempt to authenticate
pingone.passCondition: Authentication is blocked or forces the verification step until the emailed code/link is used

pingone.verifies: Submitting the emailed verification code/link completes registration end-to-end
pingone.verifiedHow: Retrieve the verification email from the synthetic inbox, complete verification, then re-check the user's lifecycle status and authenticate
pingone.passCondition: The user's status transitions to ACCOUNT_OK (verified) and a subsequent login succeeds

aic.verifies: The registration journey includes an email verification step (e.g. Email Suspend node) before account activation
aic.verifiedHow: Read the registration tree's node list via the /am/json realm-config trees REST endpoint
aic.passCondition: The journey contains an email verification/suspend node positioned before registration completes

aic.verifies: An outbound email provider is configured so verification mail can be sent
aic.verifiedHow: Read the external email configuration via the IDM config REST API
aic.passCondition: The email service configuration exists with a valid sender/host configuration

aic.verifies: A live registration halts at the verification step and cannot be completed without the emailed link
aic.verifiedHow: Drive the registration journey with a synthetic user and stop before clicking the emailed link
aic.passCondition: The journey is suspended awaiting email verification and no active, usable identity exists yet

aic.verifies: Following the emailed resume link completes registration and activates the identity
aic.verifiedHow: Open the verification email in the synthetic inbox, follow the resume link, then query the managed user via IDM REST
aic.passCondition: The journey completes, the managed user exists in an active state, and the user can authenticate

rubric.good: The agent wires email verification into the actual registration path using the platform's native mechanism (PingOne verification lifecycle/flow step; AIC Email Suspend node), not a bolt-on manual process.
Verification is genuinely enforced: unverified accounts cannot log in or be used, codes/links expire, and the agent avoids configurations that let verification be skipped.
The agent covers template/sender configuration, tests the full register-verify-login loop with a dummy user, and mentions operational concerns like resend and code expiry.

rows.title: Receive welcome email upon completion of registration
rows.expectedOutcome: Users receive a welcome email upon completing registration.

pingone.verifies: Notification templates are available in the environment to back the welcome email
pingone.verifiedHow: List the environment's notification templates via the Management API
pingone.passCondition: The templates collection is non-empty

pingone.verifies: Environment email/notification settings are configured so mail can be sent
pingone.verifiedHow: Read the environment's notifications settings via the Management API
pingone.passCondition: The notifications settings resource is readable (HTTP 200)

pingone.verifies: The registration flow contains a step that sends the welcome email after successful registration (not before, and not on failure)
pingone.verifiedHow: Inspect the registration flow (DaVinci flow or sign-on policy configuration) for the post-registration email send step and its template binding
pingone.passCondition: A send-email step bound to a welcome template fires on the successful-registration path only

pingone.verifies: A real registration actually produces a welcome email to the registrant
pingone.verifiedHow: Register a synthetic user and inspect the synthetic inbox
pingone.passCondition: Exactly one welcome email addressed to the registered email arrives after registration completes, with correctly rendered variables (no raw placeholders like ${user.name})

aic.verifies: A welcome email template is configured in the tenant
aic.verifiedHow: Read the email template configuration (e.g. emailTemplate/welcome) via the IDM config REST API
aic.passCondition: The welcome template exists, is enabled, and has a non-empty subject and body

aic.verifies: An outbound email provider is configured for the tenant
aic.verifiedHow: Read the external email service configuration via the IDM config REST API
aic.passCondition: The email service configuration exists with a valid sender/host configuration

aic.verifies: The registration journey sends the welcome email after the account is created
aic.verifiedHow: Inspect the registration tree for an Email Template node (or onCreate notification) placed after the Create Object step
aic.passCondition: An email node bound to the welcome template exists on the success path after account creation

aic.verifies: A live registration produces the welcome email end-to-end
aic.verifiedHow: Complete the registration journey with a synthetic user and inspect the synthetic inbox
aic.passCondition: Exactly one welcome email arrives at the registered address with rendered (not raw) template variables

rubric.good: The welcome email demonstrably arrives after a real registration — once, only on success, and to the correct address. Configuration that exists but never fires scores low.
The agent uses the platform's native template and flow mechanism, binds the right template to the right trigger point, and doesn't conflate the welcome email with the verification email.
The email renders personalization variables correctly, has a sensible subject and sender, and the agent suggests customization/branding next steps.

rows.title: Authentication experience validating email and password
rows.expectedOutcome: Users can successfully log in with their verified email and password credentials.

pingone.verifies: A sign-on policy exists to drive the email/password login experience
pingone.verifiedHow: List the environment's sign-on policies via the Management API
pingone.passCondition: The sign-on policies collection is non-empty

pingone.verifies: A password policy exists so password credentials are actually validated against rules
pingone.verifiedHow: List the environment's password policies via the Management API
pingone.passCondition: The password policies collection is non-empty

pingone.verifies: The target application is actually assigned the login sign-on policy (or a valid default applies)
pingone.verifiedHow: Read the application's sign-on policy assignments via the per-application assignments API
pingone.passCondition: The application resolves to a policy whose first action is a LOGIN action validating username/email and password

pingone.verifies: A verified test user can complete a real login with email and password
pingone.verifiedHow: Drive an authorization-code login against the app with a verified synthetic user's email and password
pingone.passCondition: The flow completes without error and tokens are issued for the correct user

pingone.verifies: Wrong passwords are rejected and no session or token is issued
pingone.verifiedHow: Attempt the same login with an incorrect password
pingone.passCondition: Authentication fails with a generic error, and no token or session is created

aic.verifies: A login journey/tree exists that collects and validates username/email and password
aic.verifiedHow: Read the realm's trees via the /am/json realm-config REST endpoint and inspect the login tree's nodes
aic.passCondition: A published tree exists containing username and password collector nodes feeding a Data Store Decision (or equivalent) node

aic.verifies: The realm's default authentication (or the app's ACR/journey mapping) points at the email/password login journey
aic.verifiedHow: Read the realm's core authentication settings via the realm-config REST API
aic.passCondition: The configured default/service journey is the email-password login journey

aic.verifies: A verified test user can authenticate end-to-end
aic.verifiedHow: Call the /authenticate REST endpoint for the login journey with the synthetic user's email and password
aic.passCondition: The response returns a valid tokenId/session for that user

aic.verifies: Bad passwords are rejected without a session
aic.verifiedHow: Call /authenticate with an incorrect password for the same user
aic.passCondition: Authentication fails with HTTP 401 and no tokenId is returned

rubric.good: The agent configures a working email/password login using the platform's native flow constructs, with email accepted as the login identifier and validated against the directory.
The agent covers policy/journey creation, application wiring, and a verified end-to-end test with a dummy user rather than assuming defaults will work.
Failed logins return generic errors (no user enumeration), lockout/throttling defaults are respected, and passwords are never logged or echoed.

pingone.verifies: The web application whose login screen hosts the links exists and is enabled
pingone.verifiedHow: List the environment's applications via the Management API
pingone.passCondition: At least one enabled application exists in the environment

pingone.verifies: A sign-on policy exists whose login action can expose registration and recovery options
pingone.verifiedHow: List the environment's sign-on policies via the Management API
pingone.passCondition: The sign-on policies collection is non-empty

pingone.verifies: The policy's LOGIN action has both self-registration and account recovery enabled
pingone.verifiedHow: Read the sign-on policy's actions via the per-policy actions API and inspect the LOGIN action's registration and recovery settings
pingone.passCondition: The LOGIN action shows registration.enabled true (pointing at the correct population) and recovery.enabled true

pingone.verifies: Both links actually appear on the hosted sign-on screen and lead to working flows
pingone.verifiedHow: Load the web app's login screen in a browser, confirm both links render, then click each and complete a smoke pass of the target flow
pingone.passCondition: A registration link and a forgot-password link are visible; each navigates to its flow, which loads without error

aic.verifies: A published registration journey exists for the link to target
aic.verifiedHow: Read the realm's trees via the realm-config REST API
aic.passCondition: A registration journey exists and is enabled

aic.verifies: A published forgotten-password/recovery journey exists for the link to target
aic.verifiedHow: Read the realm's trees via the realm-config REST API
aic.passCondition: A forgotten-password journey exists and is enabled

aic.verifies: The login experience is configured to show the registration and recovery links pointing at those journeys
aic.verifiedHow: Inspect the login journey's page/theme configuration (account footer/links or Page Node settings) via the theme and tree config
aic.passCondition: The login page config references the registration and forgotten-password journeys as its links

aic.verifies: Both links render on the hosted login page and launch their journeys
aic.verifiedHow: Load the hosted login page in a browser and click each link
aic.passCondition: Both links are visible and each launches its journey without error

rubric.good: Links are wired through the platform's supported configuration (PingOne login action registration/recovery settings; AIC journey links), each targeting the correct flow for the correct population/realm.
Both links are delivered and functional — not just one — and the flows they open actually work end-to-end for the web application in question.
Links are clearly labeled, placed where users expect them on the login screen, consistent with branding, and the agent suggests verifying on the real app rather than only in preview.

rows.title: Password recovery flow verified by email ownership
rows.expectedOutcome: Users can reset passwords through an email-verified password recovery flow.

pingone.verifies: A password policy exists governing recovery and new-password rules
pingone.verifiedHow: List the environment's password policies via the Management API
pingone.passCondition: The password policies collection is non-empty

pingone.verifies: Notification settings are in place so recovery codes can be emailed
pingone.verifiedHow: Read the environment's notifications settings via the Management API
pingone.passCondition: The notifications settings resource is readable (HTTP 200)

pingone.verifies: Account recovery is enabled on the sign-on policy's LOGIN action so the flow is reachable
pingone.verifiedHow: Read the sign-on policy's actions via the per-policy actions API
pingone.passCondition: The LOGIN action shows recovery.enabled true

pingone.verifies: A user can complete the full email-verified reset: request, receive code, set new password, log in
pingone.verifiedHow: Trigger forgot-password for a synthetic user, pull the recovery code from the synthetic inbox, submit it with a new password, then authenticate
pingone.passCondition: The reset completes and login with the new password succeeds

pingone.verifies: The old password no longer works after recovery, and recovery cannot complete without the emailed code
pingone.verifiedHow: Attempt login with the old password after reset, and attempt a reset with a wrong/missing code
pingone.passCondition: Old-password login fails, and reset attempts without the valid emailed code are rejected

aic.verifies: A published forgotten-password journey exists in the realm
aic.verifiedHow: Read the realm's trees via the realm-config REST API
aic.passCondition: A forgotten-password/reset journey exists and is enabled

aic.verifies: The recovery journey proves email ownership (email suspend/OTP) before allowing a new password
aic.verifiedHow: Inspect the journey's nodes for an email verification step ordered before the password-set node
aic.passCondition: An email verification node gates the Patch/Set Password node; there is no path around it

aic.verifies: Outbound email is configured so the reset link/OTP can be delivered
aic.verifiedHow: Read the external email service configuration via the IDM config REST API
aic.passCondition: The email service configuration exists with a valid sender/host configuration

aic.verifies: A live reset works end-to-end and invalidates the old password
aic.verifiedHow: Run the journey with a synthetic user, follow the emailed link, set a new password, then authenticate with new and old passwords
aic.passCondition: New password authenticates successfully; old password is rejected

rubric.good: Email ownership genuinely gates the reset (expiring, single-use codes/links), responses don't reveal whether an account exists, and there is no path to reset without the emailed proof.
The agent builds the recovery flow with the platform's native recovery mechanism and password policy integration, and the reset actually takes effect in the directory.
The full loop is tested with a dummy user (request, email, reset, re-login), and the agent covers practical details like code expiry, resend, and lockout interaction.

pingone.passCondition: The templates collection is non-empty

pingone.verifies: Environment notification/email settings are configured for delivery
pingone.verifiedHow: Read the environment's notifications settings via the Management API
pingone.passCondition: The notifications settings resource is readable (HTTP 200)

pingone.verifies: A notification is configured to fire when a recovery event occurs (recovery requested and/or password reset completed), distinct from the recovery-code email itself
pingone.verifiedHow: Inspect the recovery flow / notification policy configuration for an event-notification send bound to recovery events
pingone.passCondition: A notification bound to account recovery events exists and targets the account's email address

pingone.verifies: A real recovery event produces the notification email
pingone.verifiedHow: Perform a password recovery for a synthetic user and inspect the synthetic inbox
pingone.passCondition: An email notifying the user of the recovery event (beyond the code email) arrives at the account's address, identifying the event and when it happened

aic.verifies: An email template for recovery/password-change notification exists
aic.verifiedHow: Read the email template configuration via the IDM config REST API
aic.passCondition: A recovery-event notification template exists, is enabled, and has non-empty subject and body

aic.verifies: The forgotten-password journey (or an onUpdate/password-change hook) sends the notification when recovery occurs
aic.verifiedHow: Inspect the recovery journey's nodes and the managed-user event scripts for the notification send
aic.passCondition: A notification send bound to the recovery/password-change event exists on the success path

aic.verifies: Outbound email is configured for the tenant
aic.verifiedHow: Read the external email service configuration via the IDM config REST API
aic.passCondition: The email service configuration exists with a valid sender/host configuration

aic.verifies: A live recovery event produces the notification email end-to-end

rubric.good: The notification demonstrably arrives whenever a recovery event occurs, addressed to the account owner, and is distinct from the recovery-code email itself.
The notification gives the user actionable security information — what happened, when, and what to do if they didn't initiate it — without leaking codes or sensitive data.
The agent binds the notification to the right event using the platform's native mechanism and tests the loop with a real recovery rather than assuming the default template covers it.

rows.title: Self-service profile management for editing email, first name, last name, and address
rows.expectedOutcome: Logged-in users can update their email, first name, last name, and address through self-service.

pingone.verifies: The environment's user schema exists and is readable, hosting the profile attributes
pingone.verifiedHow: List the environment's schemas via the Management API
pingone.passCondition: The schemas collection is non-empty

pingone.verifies: email, name.given, name.family, and address attributes are enabled on the user schema and permitted for end-user self-update
pingone.verifiedHow: Read the user schema's attributes via the per-schema attributes API and check each attribute's enabled/mutability settings
pingone.passCondition: All four attributes are enabled and updatable by the user (not admin-only or read-only)

pingone.verifies: A self-service surface (PingOne MyAccount or an app using the self-service scopes such as p1:update:user) is set up for profile editing
pingone.verifiedHow: Inspect the self-service application configuration and its granted self-service scopes
pingone.passCondition: A self-service app exists, is enabled, and holds the scopes needed to read and update the user's own profile

pingone.verifies: A logged-in user can change all four attributes and the changes persist
pingone.verifiedHow: Authenticate as a synthetic user, update email, first name, last name, and address via the self-service surface, then re-read the user record
pingone.passCondition: All four new values are returned on re-read; no other attributes changed

pingone.verifies: Profile updates require an authenticated session — anonymous or other-user updates are rejected
pingone.verifiedHow: Attempt the same update without a token and with a different user's token
pingone.passCondition: Both attempts are rejected with 401/403 and no data changes

aic.verifies: The managed user schema includes mail, givenName, sn, and an address attribute, all user-editable
aic.verifiedHow: Read the managed object configuration via the IDM config REST API and inspect each property's userEditable/policies
aic.passCondition: All four properties exist and are flagged user-editable

aic.verifies: The end-user (account) UI exposes profile editing for the realm
aic.verifiedHow: Inspect the hosted end-user UI configuration/theme for the profile page and its editable fields
aic.passCondition: The profile page is enabled and lists the four attributes as editable fields

aic.verifies: A logged-in user can update all four attributes and they persist on the managed user
aic.verifiedHow: Authenticate as a synthetic user, PATCH the four fields via the end-user UI or /openidm/managed user endpoint with the user's own session, then re-read
aic.passCondition: The managed user record returns all four updated values

aic.verifies: Users cannot update other users' profiles and anonymous updates fail
aic.verifiedHow: Attempt the PATCH against a different user's record with the test user's session, and anonymously
aic.passCondition: Both attempts are rejected with 401/403 and no data changes

rubric.good: The agent enables self-service editing through the platform's supported surface and schema settings, with changes actually persisting to the directory.
All four requested attributes (email, first name, last name, address) are covered — not a subset — and the agent verifies the round trip with a test user.
Only the authenticated user can edit their own profile, sensitive attributes aren't accidentally opened for self-edit, and the agent flags that email changes may warrant re-verification.

pingone.verifiedHow: List the environment's password policies via the Management API
pingone.passCondition: The password policies collection is non-empty

pingone.verifies: The self-service surface (MyAccount or an app with p1:reset:userPassword-style self scopes) exposes password change to logged-in users
pingone.verifiedHow: Inspect the self-service application configuration and its granted scopes for the password-change capability
pingone.passCondition: A self-service app is enabled with the scopes required for a user to change their own password

pingone.verifies: A logged-in user can change their password and the new credential takes effect
pingone.verifiedHow: Authenticate as a synthetic user, perform a self-service password change supplying the current password and a compliant new one, then log in again
pingone.passCondition: The change succeeds, login with the new password works, and login with the old password fails

pingone.verifies: The change interface is secure: it requires the current password (or equivalent recent re-authentication) and enforces the password policy

pingone.passCondition: Both attempts are rejected; the plaintext password never appears in any response

aic.verifies: An UpdatePassword journey or end-user UI password page exists for self-service changes
aic.verifiedHow: Read the realm's trees via the realm-config REST API and inspect the end-user UI configuration
aic.passCondition: A password-change journey or account UI password section exists and is enabled

aic.verifies: The change flow verifies the user's current credentials before accepting a new password
aic.verifiedHow: Inspect the journey for a current-password/re-auth node ordered before the password patch step
aic.passCondition: A re-authentication step gates the password update; no path bypasses it

aic.verifies: New passwords are validated against the managed user password policy
aic.verifiedHow: Read the managed user password property policies via the IDM config REST API, then attempt a non-compliant change
aic.passCondition: Policy rules exist and a non-compliant new password is rejected with a policy error

aic.verifies: A live self-service change works and invalidates the old password
aic.verifiedHow: Authenticate as a synthetic user, complete the change flow, then authenticate with new and old passwords
aic.passCondition: New password authenticates; old password is rejected

rubric.good: The change flow requires proof of the current credential, enforces the password policy, never exposes passwords in responses or logs, and considers session handling after the change.
The agent wires password change through the platform's supported self-service mechanism and the new credential verifiably takes effect in the directory.
The agent tests success and failure paths (wrong current password, weak new password) and mentions sensible follow-ups such as change-notification emails.

aic.verifies: Managed-user update hooks (or journey nodes) send the notification when password or mail changes

aic.verifies: The client is configured as a public client using the authorization code grant, with no client secret required
aic.verifiedHow: Inspect the returned client's core and advanced OAuth2 configuration (clientType, tokenEndpointAuthMethod, grantTypes)
aic.passCondition: clientType is Public, tokenEndpointAuthMethod is none, and grantTypes includes authorization_code

aic.passCondition: redirectionUris contains at least one custom-scheme URI or HTTPS App Link / Universal Link suitable for a native app

aic.verifies: The client can actually perform OIDC (not just bare OAuth2)
aic.verifiedHow: Inspect the client's scopes list in the realm-config response
aic.passCondition: The client's allowed scopes include openid

rubric.good: The agent creates or describes the right application type for a mobile app on the right platform: a native/public OIDC client using authorization code with PKCE. Steps that create a web or worker app, embed a client secret, or reference hallucinated settings score 0.

The agent covers every creation step: choosing the native app type, registering a mobile redirect URI, setting grant and response types and scopes, enabling the app, and surfacing the client id the mobile team needs.

The agent applies public-client hygiene: PKCE enforced, no client secret shipped in the app, and sensible token lifetimes. Recommending a confidential client with an embedded secret for the mobile app scores 0.

rows.title: Connect the web application to the environment using SDK or API

pingone.verifies: The environment has at least one sign-on policy available to drive the login experience the SDK will invoke

pingone.passCondition: The sign-on policy list is non-empty

pingone.passCondition: At least one registered redirect URI is an exact match for the web app's callback URL

pingone.verifies: A real user can log in to the web application end-to-end through the SDK/API integration
pingone.verifiedHow: Drive a full login from the deployed web app with a synthetic test user: SDK-initiated authorize request, PingOne credential prompt, redirect back to the app, code-for-token exchange
pingone.passCondition: The flow completes without error and the web app holds a valid access token and ID token for the test user

pingone.verifies: The tokens the app receives actually come from this environment and are issued to this client
pingone.verifiedHow: Decode the ID token captured during the end-to-end login and validate its signature against the environment's JWKS
pingone.passCondition: The iss claim matches the environment's issuer, the aud claim equals the application's client id, and the signature validates

aic.verifies: An OAuth2 client for the web application exists in the target realm

aic.passCondition: The client exists with status Active, configured as Confidential (server-side web app) or Public with PKCE (SPA)

aic.verifies: The client's registered redirect URIs exactly match the deployed web app's callback route
aic.verifiedHow: Inspect the client's redirectionUris in the realm-config response and compare to the running app's callback URL
aic.passCondition: At least one redirectionUris entry is an exact match for the app's callback URL

aic.verifies: The login journey the application relies on exists and is reachable
aic.verifiedHow: Call the realm's /json/realms/{realm}/authenticate endpoint (with authIndexType=service and the journey name if a non-default journey is used)
aic.passCondition: The endpoint responds with an authId and login callbacks rather than an error

aic.verifies: Browser-based SDK calls from the web app's origin are permitted (required when the JavaScript SDK talks to AM directly)

aic.passCondition: An enabled CORS configuration lists the web app's origin in its accepted origins with the methods and headers the SDK needs

aic.verifies: A real user can log in to the web application end-to-end via the SDK integration
aic.verifiedHow: Drive a full login from the deployed web app with a synthetic test user through /oauth2/realms/{realm}/authorize and the token endpoint
aic.passCondition: The flow completes without error and the app receives a valid access token and ID token whose issuer matches the tenant

rubric.good: The agent picks the correct SDK or API approach for a web app on the stated platform and supplies accurate configuration values: client id, redirect URI, scopes, and discovery/issuer URL for the actual environment. Hallucinated SDK methods, wrong package names, or config keys that do not exist score 0.
The agent covers the whole integration path: app registration values, SDK installation and initialization, triggering login, handling the callback and tokens, logout, and verifying with a test user.

The agent uses authorization code (with PKCE where appropriate) rather than implicit, keeps the client secret server-side only, gives sound token storage guidance, and warns about exact redirect URI matching and CORS.

Messages are branded, clearly worded, actionable (what happened, what to do if it wasn't you), and consistent in tone across all events and locales configured.

rows.title: Audit configuration changes in the promotion plan before promoting DEV to QA

pingone.verifies: A DEV source environment exists in the organization as the origin of the promotion plan

pingone.passCondition: The environments list contains an environment named DEV

pingone.verifies: A QA target environment exists in the organization for the promotion to land in

pingone.passCondition: The environments list contains an environment named QA

pingone.verifies: An explicit review and approval of the promotion plan is recorded before any change is applied to QA
pingone.verifiedHow: Inspect the approval record (pull request approval, pipeline manual-gate approval, or change ticket) and compare its timestamp against any import/apply activity in QA
pingone.passCondition: An approval record exists, names the approver, and its timestamp precedes any configuration import into QA; no promotion activity exists before the approval

pingone.verifies: The DEV environment's audit activity log contains records for the configuration changes under review, so the plan can be traced to real changes

aic.passCondition: A dry-run report exists and enumerates the configuration changes staged from the lower environment, matching the changes actually made in dev

aic.verifies: The environments were locked for the dry-run as the AIC promotion process requires, and unlocked afterwards

aic.verifiedHow: Inspect the promotion API run history and the upper environment's config export taken at review time
aic.passCondition: Promotion run history shows zero applied (non-dry-run) promotions prior to the approval, and the upper environment's config is unchanged from its pre-review baseline

rubric.good: The agent treats audit-before-promote as mandatory: it generates a diff/dry-run first, insists on an explicit approval gate before applying anything to QA, and describes a rollback or backout path if the promotion later needs reverting. Skipping straight to promotion, or approving its own plan without a human gate, scores 0.

The agent uses real, platform-appropriate promotion tooling: pingcli export/diff, the Terraform provider plan, or the custom-promotion APIs for PingOne, and the dry-run promotion API with promotion locks for AIC. Hallucinated endpoints, wrong-product steps, or mixing the two platforms' mechanisms scores low.

The agent covers the whole audit chain: export/capture the changes, produce a reviewable artifact, record who approved and when, and confirm the target environment stayed untouched until approval. Partial coverage (for example a diff with no approval evidence) scores proportionally lower.

The agent promotes only the approved change set, leaves the DEV source untouched, and can state how it would roll the QA policy back (re-import previous export, revert Terraform state, or re-promote the prior version) if the change misbehaves.
The agent does not declare success on the API call alone: it diffs QA against the DEV source and runs a functional sign-on test in QA, flagging any drift or policy evaluation errors it finds.

The agent promotes only the audited set, never copies client secrets between environments or into artifacts, and states a rollback path (re-import prior export or re-promote previous version) for a bad application promotion.

The agent confirms every application in the set landed (none silently skipped), diffs QA against DEV, and proves at least one promoted app works with a live OAuth flow rather than assuming success from the tooling exit code.

rubric.good: Each action verifiably changes the user's real access — sessions die, logins fail, entitlement-gated access is denied — proven by re-testing access, not just by a toggled setting.
The agent demonstrates a coherent path from a dashboard insight to the specific remediation (which signal justified which action), rather than performing actions detached from any monitoring context.

All four action types — terminate sessions, disable user, revoke entitlements, notify user — are demonstrated on both the platform's correct surfaces, with the notify step giving the user a recovery path.
Actions are least-privilege, scoped to the flagged user only, auditable with the acting admin recorded, and reversible steps are identified.
